scope: Pediatric outpatient/home medication regimens after ED/urgent-care evaluation
safety_rules: Select regimen by diagnosis; never copy a dose across indications.
Liquid mL may be generated only from an explicitly verified exact product concentration.
Apply source adult/per-dose and daily caps.
Weight basis is explicit. Do not substitute actual/ideal/adjusted weight silently.
Marked obesity requires drug-specific review when evidence is limited; adult maximums still apply when the source specifies them.
Renal/hepatic impairment, allergy, drug interactions, inability to tolerate oral treatment, red flags and age restrictions may override outpatient treatment.

obesity_policy.rule: For patients <18 years and <40 kg, weight-based dosing is generally used. At >=40 kg, continue weight-based dosing unless it exceeds the recommended adult dose for the indication. Drug-specific PK/weight-scalar evidence supersedes this general rule.
obesity_policy.explicit_exception: RCH oral paracetamol is dosed on ideal body weight.
obesity_policy.note: Do not assign ideal or adjusted body weight to other outpatient drugs without drug-specific evidence.

entries.diagnosis: mild/moderate pain or fever in a child >1 month suitable for home treatment
entries.frequency: every 6 h as needed; minimum interval 4 h
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food. Shake suspension. Avoid all other paracetamol/acetaminophen-containing products.
entries.source: RCH Acute Pain Management 2024; current paracetamol SmPC 120 mg/5 mL

entries.diagnosis: mild/moderate pain or fever when NSAID is appropriate
entries.frequency: every 6-8 h as needed; home schedule capped at 3 doses/day
entries.administration: Give with food; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.

excluded_patient_flags.message: avoid ibuprofen in dehydration because of renal risk
avoid/seek specialist dosing advice in significant renal impairment
contraindicated with active/recurrent peptic ulcer or GI bleeding

entries.source: RCH Acute Pain Management 2024; ibuprofen 100 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: persistent nausea/vomiting with gastroenteritis to support oral rehydration; child >6 months
entries.administration: Adjunct to oral rehydration only. Improvement in vomiting does not exclude serious disease.
cautions: bilious vomiting or surgical red flags

entries.diagnosis: isolated acute urticaria without anaphylaxis, age 6-11 months
entries.administration: Use a non-sedating antihistamine. Avoid NSAIDs as they can worsen urticaria.
cautions: any airway/respiratory/circulatory or significant GI involvement = evaluate for anaphylaxis
entries.source: RCH Urticaria; current cetirizine product concentration

entries.diagnosis: isolated acute urticaria/allergic symptoms, age >=1 year
entries.administration: May be given as oral solution. Avoid NSAIDs in acute urticaria if they worsen symptoms.
cautions: anaphylaxis features require adrenaline pathway, not antihistamine alone

entries.diagnosis: allergic rhinitis or urticaria, age >=2 years
entries.administration: Oral syrup. In severe hepatic impairment use the product-label reduced initial frequency rather than this standard regimen.

entries.diagnosis: allergic rhinitis or urticaria, age >=1 year
seasonal allergic rhinitis when fexofenadine selected
entries.administration: For the 120 mg adolescent tablet regimen, take before a meal. Product/age licensing varies; verify exact product.

entries.diagnosis: moderately severe/severe asthma exacerbation suitable for discharge, age <2 years
entries.administration: Give according to written asthma discharge plan; food may reduce GI upset if product permits.

entries.diagnosis: moderately severe/severe asthma exacerbation suitable for discharge, age 2-5 years
acute asthma exacerbation suitable for discharge, age 6-11 years
acute asthma exacerbation when dexamethasone strategy selected
croup with stridor/risk features suitable for outpatient management after assessment
asthma/wheeze discharge reliever via pMDI + spacer under written asthma action plan
entries.frequency: per written asthma action plan; urgent review if reliever is required again within 4 h after discharge
entries.administration: One puff at a time through spacer with correct technique. Ensure written action plan and controller review.
entries.source: RCH asthma discharge education; GINA 2026 acute asthma

entries.diagnosis: acute otitis media when antibiotic treatment is indicated
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food; follow exact product label. Complete the prescribed course.

entries.diagnosis: mild community-acquired pneumonia treated as outpatient
dental abscess requiring antibiotic plus dental/surgical management
entries.administration: Antibiotic does not replace definitive dental/surgical treatment.

entries.diagnosis: infected/high-risk bite suitable for oral outpatient therapy

verified_concentrations.label: 400/57 mg per 5 mL; amoxicillin component 80 mg/mL

entries.administration: Give at the start of a meal; shake suspension before each dose.
entries.source: RCH antimicrobial bite regimen + co-amoxiclav 400/57 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: periorbital/orbital cellulitis oral step-down after appropriate initial assessment/treatment
entries.administration: Give at the start of a meal. Not a substitute for orbital-cellulitis imaging/specialist/inpatient pathway when indicated.

entries.diagnosis: mild/moderate cellulitis suitable for oral outpatient therapy
entries.administration: May be given without regard to meals. Reassess if rapidly progressive or systemic illness.
cautions: marked renal impairment requires dose review

entries.diagnosis: mild preseptal cellulitis in a well child
uncomplicated lower UTI/cystitis in a child >3 months who is not systemically unwell
pyelonephritis in selected child <12 months suitable for oral regimen per local pathway
cautions: young infant threshold for admission/IV treatment

entries.diagnosis: pyelonephritis age >=12 months suitable for oral outpatient therapy
cautions: systemic illness may require IV/inpatient care

entries.diagnosis: mild MRSA-suspected/confirmed skin infection when TMP-SMX selected

verified_concentrations.label: 40 mg TMP/200 mg SMX per 5 mL; TMP 8 mg/mL

entries.administration: Dose expressed as trimethoprim component. Taking with food or drink may reduce GI upset.
entries.source: RCH Antimicrobial guidelines; Co-Trimoxazole pediatric suspension SmPC 2026

entries.diagnosis: mild MRSA skin infection when clindamycin selected
entries.administration: Give with a full glass of water when age-appropriate; monitor for antibiotic-associated diarrhea/colitis.

entries.diagnosis: pertussis treatment/prophylaxis regimen in infant <6 months
entries.administration: Once daily, with or without food; immediately before a meal may improve GI tolerability. Shake suspension.
entries.source: RCH Antimicrobial guidelines; azithromycin 200 mg/5 mL SmPC 2026

entries.diagnosis: pertussis treatment/prophylaxis regimen age >=6 months
entries.administration: Once daily, with or without food; immediately before a meal may improve GI tolerability. Shake suspension.
entries.source: RCH Antimicrobial guidelines; azithromycin 200 mg/5 mL SmPC 2026

entries.diagnosis: pertussis when clarithromycin selected, age >=1 month
entries.administration: May be given without regard to meals; food/drink after the suspension can reduce bitter aftertaste.
cautions: renal impairment may require dose reduction
entries.source: RCH antimicrobial pertussis regimen; clarithromycin 125 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: pertussis when macrolide cannot be used, age >6 weeks

verified_concentrations.label: TMP 8 mg/mL in 40/200 mg per 5 mL suspension

entries.administration: Dose expressed as trimethoprim component. May be preferable with food/drink to reduce GI upset.
entries.source: RCH antimicrobial pertussis regimen; Co-Trimoxazole SmPC

entries.diagnosis: lower UTI/cystitis, NICE short-course variant
entries.administration: Take with food or milk; shake suspension.

minimum_patient_values.message: nitrofurantoin outpatient regimen requires eGFR >=45 mL/min in this module

excluded_patient_flags.message: nitrofurantoin is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency in the cited SmPC
nitrofurantoin is contraindicated in acute porphyria
nitrofurantoin must not be used for pyelonephritis/renal parenchymal infection

entries.source: NICE NG109 short-course lower UTI regimen; nitrofurantoin 25 mg/5 mL SmPC for product/food/contraindications

entries.diagnosis: acute lower UTI using current 25 mg/5 mL SmPC course
entries.administration: Take with food or milk; shake suspension.

minimum_patient_values.message: nitrofurantoin is contraindicated below eGFR 45 mL/min in this SmPC regimen

entries.diagnosis: influenza treatment in infant <1 year when antiviral treatment indicated
influenza treatment age >=1 year when antiviral treatment indicated
anaphylaxis discharge plan when auto-injector is indicated

bands.device: 500 microgram device may be considered in adolescents >12 years where locally available; 300 microgram device remains product/pathway dependent

entries.administration: Provide two devices when indicated, device training, written anaphylaxis action plan and allergy referral. IM adrenaline remains first-line for recurrent anaphylaxis.

entries.diagnosis: localized impetigo suitable for topical therapy
entries.topical_instructions: Apply mupirocin 2% to affected area three times daily for 5 days.

entries.diagnosis: acute otitis media when antibiotic treatment is indicated and penicillin allergy/intolerance requires a macrolide alternative
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food. Verify exact suspension strength; important CYP3A/QT interactions apply.
contraindications: concomitant contraindicated QT/CYP3A interacting medicines per SmPC
entries.source: NICE NG91 acute otitis media, amended 2022; clarithromycin SmPC for product use

entries.diagnosis: acute sinusitis in a child when immediate/back-up antibiotic is indicated and first-choice penicillin is appropriate
entries.administration: Use exact product instructions. Oral penicillin V absorption is reduced by food for many products; follow the exact SmPC and preferably dose away from meals when specified.
cautions: renal impairment may require interval review
severe systemic/orbital/intracranial features require hospital pathway

entries.diagnosis: acute sinusitis requiring antibiotic in child with penicillin allergy/intolerance
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food; verify exact formulation.

entries.diagnosis: community-acquired pneumonia in child when oral macrolide is selected for penicillin allergy/intolerance or atypical pathogen coverage
entries.administration: May be taken with or without food; verify exact product and interaction profile.
entries.source: NICE NG250 pneumonia; RCH CAP allergy pathway

entries.diagnosis: impetigo that is extensive or unsuitable for localized topical therapy
entries.administration: Can be taken without regard to meals; verify exact SmPC.

entries.diagnosis: mild bacterial cervical lymphadenitis suitable for oral outpatient therapy
preschool asthma age 1-5 years requiring first-line preventer treatment
entries.administration: Use pMDI with spacer; facemask until coordinated with mouthpiece. Rinse mouth/brush teeth after ICS where feasible. Review control and technique.
cautions: step down to lowest effective dose

entries.diagnosis: preschool asthma age 1-5 years when LTRA is chosen as alternative/adjunct preventer
entries.administration: Chewable/granule product depends on age and local product. Stop and review if agitation, sleep disturbance, mood or behavioral changes occur.
entries.source: RCH Preschool asthma; INFARMED confirms 4 mg pediatric chewable presentations in Portugal

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years, Step 2 low-dose ICS preventer
entries.administration: Use prescribed inhaler correctly; review adherence, technique and control before step-up.
entries.source: RCH asthma in primary school-aged children

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years, Step 2 low-dose ICS preventer
entries.administration: Use spacer with pMDI when appropriate; rinse mouth after ICS. Check adherence and technique before step-up.
entries.source: RCH asthma in primary school-aged children

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years when montelukast is selected as alternative/adjunct controller
entries.administration: Review for agitation, sleep disturbance or altered mood and stop/reassess if these occur.
entries.source: RCH asthma 6-11 years; INFARMED pediatric 5 mg chewable presentations

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years, Step 3 ICS/LABA maintenance option
entries.frequency: twice daily maintenance; reliever strategy must match written plan
entries.administration: Controller regimen only. Confirm whether separate SABA or MART strategy is being used; do not mix plans silently.
entries.source: RCH asthma in primary school-aged children

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 6-11 years using GINA 2026 AIR/MART strategy with the specified low-dose budesonide-formoterol formulation

bands.step3: 1 inhalation once daily plus 1 as needed
bands.step4: 1 inhalation twice daily plus 1 as needed

entries.administration: Use only the specified ICS-formoterol strength/device suitable for AIR/MART. Seek medical care if >8 total inhalations are needed in 24 h.

entries.diagnosis: asthma age 12-17 years using GINA 2026 AIR/MART strategy

bands.step3: 1 inhalation twice (or once) daily plus 1 as needed
bands.step4_5: 2 inhalations twice daily plus 1 as needed

entries.administration: AIR/MART only with an appropriate ICS-formoterol product. Seek medical care if >12 total inhalations are needed in 24 h.

entries.diagnosis: mild-to-moderate eczema flare on sensitive areas such as face/groin when a mild topical corticosteroid is appropriate
entries.topical_instructions: Apply a thin appropriate amount to affected eczema twice daily until the flare is resolved. Use ointment where practical for emollient effect; avoid prolonged unsupervised treatment.
contraindications: untreated primary bacterial/fungal/viral skin infection at treatment site unless separately treated
entries.portugal_reconciliation: INFARMED lists hydrocortisone 10 mg/g topical strength in Portugal; pediatric indication/product-specific RCM and Azores stock still require exact product verification.

entries.diagnosis: mild-to-moderate eczema flare on body requiring moderate-potency topical corticosteroid
entries.topical_instructions: Apply once daily to affected body areas until resolved; use short courses on sensitive sites only under clinician direction.

entries.diagnosis: severe eczema flare on body when a potent topical corticosteroid is appropriate
entries.topical_instructions: Apply once daily to affected body areas until resolved, using the shortest effective course. Do not use very potent steroids without dermatology advice.
cautions: skin atrophy risk with prolonged use

entries.diagnosis: mild-to-moderate eczema on sensitive areas when second-line non-steroid topical therapy is selected
entries.topical_instructions: Apply twice daily until symptoms resolve. Limit treatment to 6 weeks; for age 3-23 months limit course to 3 weeks per cited RCH guidance.
cautions: avoid application to active untreated infection

entries.diagnosis: scabies in a child suitable for topical treatment
entries.topical_instructions: Apply as directed to the entire appropriate skin surface; RCH describes neck-down application left on for at least 8 hours, usually overnight. Repeat after 7 days if required. Treat household/close contacts simultaneously and decontaminate clothing/bedding per local advice.
entries.frequency: single application; repeat after 7 days when indicated
cautions: infants/young children may require head/neck/scalp application per product/local guideline

entries.diagnosis: localized tinea corporis/cruris or other susceptible superficial dermatophyte infection excluding scalp/nail disease
entries.topical_instructions: Apply a thin layer to affected and surrounding skin 2-3 times daily. Continue for at least 1 month for dermatophyte infection according to the cited SmPC. Keep skin clean and dry.
cautions: do not use for scalp or nail infection

entries.diagnosis: localized cutaneous candidal infection including candidal intertrigo/nappy rash when antifungal therapy is indicated
entries.topical_instructions: Apply thinly and evenly 2-3 times daily; continue for at least 2 weeks for candidal infection per SmPC.
cautions: persistent diaper rash needs diagnostic reassessment

entries.diagnosis: gastroenteritis with clinical dehydration suitable for oral rehydration
entries.frequency: frequent small amounts over 4 hours plus maintenance/ongoing losses
entries.administration: Use low-osmolarity ORS 240-250 mOsm/L. Give frequently in small amounts; continue breastfeeding. Avoid fruit juice/carbonated drinks during rehydration. Add maintenance fluid and replace ongoing losses.

excluded_patient_flags.message: oral-only rehydration regimen is not appropriate when IV resuscitation/rehydration is indicated

entries.diagnosis: replacement after a large watery stool in a child at increased risk of recurrent dehydration after rehydration
entries.administration: Give 5 mL/kg after each large watery stool when risk of recurrent dehydration is increased. Continue usual feeding after rehydration.

entries.diagnosis: chronic idiopathic constipation maintenance in child 1-11 years after assessment for impaction/red flags
entries.frequency: daily; titrate to regular soft stools
entries.administration: For the referenced paediatric formulation each sachet contains macrogol 3350 6.563 g with electrolytes and is reconstituted in 62.5 mL water. Adjust dose to response; do not stop abruptly after prolonged treatment.
contraindications: severe inflammatory bowel disease/toxic megacolon per product SmPC
entries.source: NICE CG99 + Movicol Paediatric Plain 6.9 g SmPC

entries.diagnosis: faecal impaction in child 5-11 years when oral macrogol disimpaction is appropriate
entries.frequency: daily total divided and consumed within 12 hours
entries.administration: Each referenced paediatric sachet is reconstituted in 62.5 mL water. Stop escalation/course once disimpaction has occurred and transition to maintenance plan.
cautions: not recommended by cited SmPC for faecal impaction with impaired cardiovascular function or renal insufficiency

entries.diagnosis: constipation when lactulose is selected because macrogol is unsuitable/not tolerated or as an adjunct according to the constipation plan
entries.frequency: twice daily in the NICE pediatric ranges; titrate according to response
entries.administration: May be taken diluted or undiluted; may be taken with water or fruit juice. Maintain adequate fluid intake. Effect may take 2-3 days. Select the actual volume within the age-band range according to response; the engine does not choose it automatically.
cautions: contains manufacturing residues of lactose/galactose/fructose; check relevant intolerances
entries.source: NICE CG99 plus Duphalac 3.335 g/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: confirmed/suspected Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) in child age >=2 years after household hygiene plan

verified_concentrations.label: 400 mg/20 mL oral suspension (Zentel strength documented in Portugal product information; current local stock still requires Infomed/Azores confirmation)

entries.frequency: single dose, repeat once after 2 weeks
entries.administration: Take on an empty stomach for pinworm per CDC. Treat household/caregiver contacts simultaneously when clinically appropriate and reinforce hand hygiene, bathing, laundering and nail hygiene.
cautions: children <2 years require individualized risk-benefit assessment rather than this regimen
entries.source: CDC Pinworm Clinical Overview 2024; INFARMED product-strength documentation

entries.diagnosis: confirmed/suspected Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) in child age >=2 years
entries.frequency: single dose, repeat once after 2 weeks
entries.administration: Second dose is required because treatment kills worms but not eggs. Combine with household hygiene measures.
cautions: children <2 years require individualized risk-benefit assessment

entries.diagnosis: confirmed/suspected Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) in child age >=2 years when pyrantel is selected
entries.frequency: single dose, repeat once after 2 weeks
entries.administration: Verify exact salt/base convention and suspension concentration before calculating mL; concentrations vary by product.
cautions: children <2 years require individualized risk-benefit assessment

entries.diagnosis: uncomplicated acute/chronic strongyloidiasis with confirmed clinical indication in child weighing >=15 kg

minimum_patient_values.message: CDC lists weight <15 kg as a relative contraindication for ivermectin strongyloidiasis treatment

excluded_patient_flags.message: ivermectin is relatively contraindicated with suspected/confirmed concomitant Loa loa infection

entries.administration: Oral ivermectin; verify exact tablet strength and local product instructions. Follow-up stool examination is recommended if symptoms persist with initially positive stool testing.

entries.diagnosis: ascariasis in child age >=2 years when albendazole is selected

verified_concentrations.label: 400 mg/20 mL oral suspension strength documented in Portugal; verify current exact product

entries.administration: Take on an empty stomach for ascariasis per CDC.

entries.diagnosis: Schistosoma mansoni/S. haematobium/S. intercalatum infection in child age >=4 years under a confirmed treatment plan
entries.frequency: two divided doses over one day
entries.administration: Take with liquid during a meal. CDC notes limited trial safety data below age 4, although WHO mass-drug-administration recommendations include younger children in some settings.
cautions: species must be identified because S. japonicum/S. mekongi require a different 60 mg/kg/day regimen
consider repeat treatment 2-4 weeks later in selected light infections

entries.diagnosis: varicella in a child when oral aciclovir treatment is clinically indicated and standard renal dosing is appropriate

required_patient_flags.message: this standard varicella regimen must not be used when renal dose adjustment is required

entries.administration: Start as early as clinically appropriate; in immunocompetent chickenpox product information advises beginning within 24 hours of rash onset. Maintain adequate hydration. Shake suspension.
cautions: immunocompromised/severe disease may require specialist/IV treatment
entries.source: Current aciclovir 200 mg/5 mL and 400 mg/5 mL SmPC

entries.diagnosis: mucocutaneous herpes simplex treatment in child when oral aciclovir is appropriate and standard renal dosing is suitable
entries.frequency: five times daily at approximately 4-hour intervals while awake

required_patient_flags.message: this standard HSV regimen must not be used when renal dose adjustment is required

entries.administration: Oral suspension; maintain hydration. Neonatal herpes and severe/immunocompromised disease are outside this outpatient regimen.

entries.diagnosis: uncomplicated bacterial conjunctivitis with purulent discharge, clear cornea and no infiltrate after red-eye assessment
entries.topical_instructions: Instil chloramphenicol 0.5% eye drops 4-6 times per day for 5-7 days, with eye toilet and hand-hygiene/infection-control measures.
cautions: unilateral red eye needs diagnostic caution
pain/photophobia/corneal infiltrate/vision change/trauma/contact-lens ulcer require ophthalmic pathway
stop if hypersensitivity and seek review

entries.drug: ciprofloxacin 3 mg/mL + dexamethasone 1 mg/mL ear drops
entries.diagnosis: acute otitis externa in child age >=1 year when this combination is selected
entries.topical_instructions: Instil 4 drops into the affected ear twice daily for 7 days. Warm suspension in the hand before use and follow product positioning instructions.
contraindications: viral or fungal otic infection per SmPC
cautions: verify tympanic membrane/diagnosis and exact product
entries.source: Ciprofloxacin/dexamethasone 3 mg/mL + 1 mg/mL ear drops SmPC

entries.diagnosis: acute otitis externa in child >1 year with intact tympanic membrane and susceptible organisms
entries.topical_instructions: Instil one 0.25 mL single-dose ampoule into the affected ear twice daily for 7 days. Warm ampoule in the hand; keep affected ear upward about 5 minutes after instillation.
cautions: this product indication specifies intact tympanic membrane

entries.drug: phenazone 40 mg/g + lidocaine 10 mg/g ear drops
entries.diagnosis: acute otitis media pain when immediate oral antibiotic is not given and there is no tympanic membrane perforation or otorrhoea
entries.topical_instructions: Apply 4 drops to the affected ear 2-3 times daily for up to 7 days.

excluded_patient_flags.message: NICE analgesic ear-drop option is for cases where an immediate oral antibiotic is not given
do not use this phenazone/lidocaine regimen with tympanic membrane perforation or otorrhoea

entries.source: NICE NG91 acute otitis media, amended 2022

entries.diagnosis: migraine in child >6 years when oral simple analgesics are ineffective and rizatriptan is selected

bands.note: may repeat once after at least 2 hours if headache recurs; max 2 doses/24h
source states >40 kg; exact 40 kg intentionally left unmatched/fail-closed

entries.frequency: single dose early in migraine; may repeat once after >=2 h if recurrence; max 2 doses/24 h
entries.administration: Use after simple oral analgesics are ineffective. Maintain hydration/rest in dark quiet environment. Avoid opioids.
cautions: propranolol increases rizatriptan concentration—avoid or use lower dose with specialist advice
cardiovascular contraindications/triptan interactions require product-specific screening
exactly 40 kg is unresolved by cited RCH wording and should be clinician-reviewed

entries.diagnosis: migraine with vomiting during/after ED assessment when oral ondansetron is selected
entries.frequency: single oral dose in the acute episode
entries.administration: This use is guideline-based for migraine-associated vomiting; the cited syrup SmPC concentration is used only for volume arithmetic, not to imply the migraine indication is product-licensed.
cautions: severe hepatic impairment affects total daily dose
entries.source: RCH Headache + current ondansetron 4 mg/5 mL SmPC for concentration

entries.diagnosis: head lice when dimeticone 4% topical therapy is selected
entries.topical_instructions: Apply dimeticone 4% according to the exact product directions and repeat treatment after 7 days as recommended by the cited RCH antimicrobial guidance.
cautions: treat only live infestation according to local policy

entries.diagnosis: secondary bacterial infection of eczema with localized crusting/weeping/pustules, child systemically well and suitable for oral therapy
entries.administration: Continue appropriate eczema skin care/topical anti-inflammatory treatment after crust removal unless contraindicated. Reassess if not improving.
cautions: systemic illness/severe infection may require admission/IV therapy
consider MRSA if high-risk or not responding
eczema herpeticum requires prompt antiviral pathway, not antibiotic alone
entries.source: RCH Eczema / Eczema management + RCH antimicrobial skin dosing

entries.diagnosis: seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis requiring intranasal corticosteroid

bands.maintenance_note: after control, 1 spray per nostril daily may be effective

entries.administration: Prime/use exact spray per SmPC. Aim away from nasal septum. Use regularly; full benefit may take up to 48 hours. Use lowest effective dose after control.
cautions: monitor growth with prolonged corticosteroid use
entries.source: Mometasone furoate 50 mcg/actuation SmPC; RCH allergic rhinitis
entries.portugal_reconciliation: INFARMED documentation confirms mometasone nasal 50 micrograms/dose presentations in Portugal; current exact brand/Azores stock must be checked in Infomed.

entries.diagnosis: seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis when fluticasone propionate nasal spray is selected

bands.maintenance_note: reduce to 1 spray per nostril daily when controlled

entries.frequency: once daily initially; selected patients may require product-label step-up
entries.administration: Prefer morning dosing. Use lowest effective dose and correct intranasal technique; avoid eye contact.
cautions: growth monitoring for prolonged pediatric use
CYP3A4 interactions can increase systemic corticosteroid exposure
entries.portugal_reconciliation: Portuguese market documents list fluticasone propionate 50 micrograms/dose nasal products; exact pediatric-labelled product and Azores availability require Infomed verification.

entries.diagnosis: moderate-to-severe seasonal/perennial allergic rhinitis age >=12 years when monotherapy with intranasal antihistamine or corticosteroid is insufficient

bands.device: azelastine hydrochloride 137 mcg + fluticasone propionate 50 mcg/actuation

entries.frequency: one spray in each nostril twice daily
entries.administration: Regular use is required for full benefit. Avoid contact with eyes. Shake/prime according to exact product.
cautions: not recommended below 12 years in cited SmPC

entries.diagnosis: seasonal allergic conjunctivitis age >=3 years
entries.topical_instructions: Instil 1 drop into affected eye(s) twice daily, approximately 8-hourly. Avoid touching the dropper tip. Remove contact lenses according to product instructions.
entries.administration: Ophthalmic use only. May be maintained for up to 4 months if clinically required under product guidance.
cautions: eye pain, photophobia, reduced vision or corneal signs require diagnostic reassessment
separate from other eye drops by product-recommended interval

entries.diagnosis: symptomatic seasonal allergic conjunctivitis age >=3 years
entries.topical_instructions: Instil 1 drop into affected eye(s) twice daily. Avoid touching the dropper tip and follow contact-lens instructions.
cautions: if symptoms do not improve or worsen, reassess diagnosis
benzalkonium-containing products may affect contact lenses
entries.source: Zaditen ketotifen 0.25 mg/mL SmPC 2025; INFARMED ketotifen ophthalmic protocol
entries.portugal_reconciliation: INFARMED confirms ketotifen 0.25 mg/mL ophthalmic products/protocol; a 2025 recall affected one specific Zaditen lot, not the whole active substance. Verify current product/lot/Azores stock.

entries.drug: docusate sodium 12.5 mg/5 mL oral solution
entries.diagnosis: constipation in child >6 months when docusate is specifically selected as an alternative stool-softener
entries.administration: Dilute each dose in a glass of flavoured drink such as fruit juice or milk and drink within 30 minutes of preparation. Ensure adequate fluid intake.
cautions: not first-line over macrogol in the project constipation pathway
sorbitol/fructose and phenylalanine excipient considerations depend on product

expansion_notes: Block A: diagnosis-specific antibiotic alternatives and asthma controller strategies; GINA 2026/RCH/NICE; Portugal concentrations only where independently verified.
Block B: dermatology topical therapy plus ORS/constipation regimens; source-specific product strengths and non-mg dose models.
Block C: selected antiparasitics, oral antivirals, ENT/ophthalmology therapies and migraine discharge treatments; renal and age/weight gates retained.
Block D: infected eczema, allergic rhinitis intranasal therapy, allergic conjunctivitis and selected alternative constipation therapy.
